Archival records show that mandatory piped connections and compulsory minimum water charges for buildings with rents above 100 escudos (Decreto-Lei 23:707 of 1934; Decreto 29:216 of 1938) improved public sanitation in Barreiro but created affordability barriers and widespread non-payment: unpaid bills reached nearly one-quarter of issued bills in 1942, accumulated to 125% in 1943, and reached three-quarters in 1944. Raising the mandatory-payment rent threshold to 200 escudos/month (full exemption up to 200 escudos/month and tiered minimum consumption of 2 m3 for 200-400 escudos, 3 m3 for 400-800 escudos, and 5 m3 above 800 escudos) enabled new consumer contracts in lower-income brackets from 1944.
